pain: PayPal's legacy server SDKs are deprecated or archived, yet still carry the overwhelming majority of installs - every one of those integrations is on borrowed time
audience: merchants, agencies and platforms running PayPal server integrations
evidence_source: npm registry API + pypistats.org (harvested by tools/)
quantified: paypalrestsdk (PyPI, marked Deprecated) 990,808 downloads/mo; paypalhttp 971,282/mo; @paypal/checkout-server-sdk 234,050/mo; new @paypal/paypal-server-sdk 618,851/mo; new Python Server SDK only 30,749/mo
paypal_apis_that_could_address_it: Orders v2 + JS SDK v6 + Server SDKs
notes: ~1.2M legacy Python installs per month vs 31k on the replacement. The migration has barely started.

pain: All non-Braintree PayPal server SDKs have been deprecated; developers are told to hand-roll HTTPS calls to the REST API
evidence_source: Stack Overflow accepted answers 2020-2026 + PayPal docs
quantified: multiple language SDK families retired (PHP SDK archived 2025-08-22); answers repeatedly recommend manual access_token handling
notes: 'There is no current SDK for them' is the recurring answer. A documented, years-long gap.

pain: Braintree Drop-in SDK was deprecated 1 Oct 2026 and becomes unsupported 1 Oct 2027 - a dated migration obligation for every merchant using it
audience: Braintree merchants and their dev teams
quantified: deprecation effective 2026-10-01; unsupported 2027-10-01; migration to Android/iOS/JS SDKs required
notes: A live, dated forcing function that exists now and will still be live during judging.

pain: Upgrading and certifying a merchant's PayPal integration used to require a specialist competing with the merchant's own roadmap, and took weeks
quantified: PayPal states certification 'now takes hours rather than weeks' with their internal Merchant AI Integration Agent
notes: The strongest single signal in the dataset: PayPal built this internally and described it publicly.

pain: Every additional payment gateway or version adds weeks of engineering and certification work
quantified: each new gateway adds 3-6 weeks of dev, test and certification; custom payment integrations start at $200,000
notes: Secondary evidence - use for scale context only, not as the primary claim.

pain: The replacement SDK family is brand new across six languages and adoption is minimal
quantified: 6 language SDKs (PHP, Ruby, TS, Python, Java, .NET), 7-70 stars each, pushed Aug-Oct 2026
notes: Low stars plus high legacy downloads equals a migration wave that has not happened yet.

pain: Almost half of BNPL users have paid late in the past year, and the rate has risen three years running
audience: BNPL users, skewing younger and subprime
quantified: 47% paid late in 2026 vs 41% in 2025 vs 34% in 2024; 72% of late payments were about a week late
notes: Self-reported. Pair with CFPB charge-off data to avoid overstating.

pain: Borrowers stack BNPL loans across lenders with no consolidated view of what they owe
evidence_source: CFPB 'Consumer Use of Buy Now Pay Later' (Jan 2025)
quantified: 63% held multiple simultaneous BNPL loans; 33% at multiple lenders; 20% opened more than one loan per month
notes: Stacking is the mechanism behind the late-payment trend.

pain: A BNPL payment can push a user into overdraft or NSF fees at their bank
quantified: 11% of BNPL users say a BNPL payment triggered an overdraft or NSF fee; 64% of late payers were charged extra
notes: Concrete, dollar-denominated harm.

pain: Most BNPL use is not a cash-flow optimisation - it is borrowing for something the buyer cannot afford
quantified: 68% say BNPL caused overspending; 54-59% say it was the only way they could afford the purchase
notes: This is the affordability question an agent could actually answer at checkout.

pain: PayPal's own instalment product has produced concrete user harm (late fee on a one-day-late payment)
quantified: $29 late fee incurred for a payment one day late on PayPal's 6-month plan
notes: Single case - illustrative only, not statistical.

pain: The BNPL market is large and still growing fast, so the harm scales with it
evidence_source: Federal Reserve (Jun 2026); CFPB BNPL market report (Dec 2025)
quantified: ~$160B BNPL lent in 2025; pay-in-4 up ~80% since the CFPB's prior measurement
notes: Use as market-size context.

pain: PayPal has elevated BNPL regulatory exposure relative to peers
evidence_source: CFPB orders (2021); FRBP research on BNPL credit reporting
quantified: PayPal was one of five BNPL providers ordered to produce data; PayPal reports missed payments to CRAs where Affirm/Afterpay do not
notes: Supports a responsible-BNPL framing rather than a growth framing.

pain: Cross-border remittance costs more than twice the UN target
evidence_source: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide, Issue 54 (Q3 2025)
quantified: global average 6.36% to send $200 vs SDG target of 3%; banks 14.99%; digital 4.59%
notes: Primary, authoritative, cited everywhere.

pain: The cheap option usually already exists - senders simply do not get it
quantified: cost to send $200 to India 5.30% average vs SmaRT (3 cheapest services) 3.29% - a ~2 point gap the sender keeps paying
notes: Sharpest framing available: not 'fees are high' but 'the good price exists and is not delivered'.

pain: India is the world's largest remittance recipient and still growing double digits
quantified: $144.8B in FY2025-26, up 16% from $124.6B; US 27.7% of inflows, UAE 19.2%
notes: Makes the audience concrete and enormous, specifically where you are.

pain: A sender remitting $400/month loses a meaningful annual sum to the gap between average and best-available pricing
evidence_source: derived from World Bank RPW P14/P15
quantified: 6.36% vs 3.29% on $400/mo = ~$147/year per sender
notes: Derived - show your arithmetic if you use this.

pain: Half of everything PayPal users formally complain about is money they cannot access or did not authorise
quantified: 57.3% of 18,296 complaints since 2025 are unauthorised transactions, inability to access funds, or other transaction problems
notes: The macro pain underpinning every trust framing.

pain: Formal complaints are rising fast and mostly resolve without money changing hands
quantified: 10,884 in 2026 YTD vs 7,412 in all of 2025 (+47%); 61.4% closed with explanation, only 17.1% with monetary relief
notes: Complaint volume is self-selected - cite as directional, never as a failure rate.

pain: The top five complaint categories are 68% of all filings - the pain is concentrated, not diffuse
quantified: top 5 issues = 68.3% of 18,296 complaints
notes: Concentration means a narrow product can address most of the pain.

pain: New and infrequent sellers have funds held 21 days per payment, and above a per-month early-release threshold every payment is held again - so working capital is blocked exactly when volume grows
audience: Solo sellers, contractors and micro-merchants receiving client payments
evidence_source: r/paypal + r/AusLegal + r/artbusiness threads; PayPal seller hold policy
quantified: 21 days standard; early-release threshold quoted at $173/month on one account vs a $1,453 payment; holds reported on $16,000 and $28,000 payments
frequency: Recurring; the most common single merchant complaint theme in the threads reviewed
notes: Medium strength: abundant but self-selected anecdote, no aggregate dataset. See QUALITATIVE_QUOTES.md section A.

pain: Accounts are permanently limited and funds held 180 days with no stated reason and no reachable human decision-maker; merchants report it after 10 fulfilled orders or 15 years of clean history
audience: Small merchants and sole traders whose entire cash balance sits in PayPal
evidence_source: r/paypal + r/AusLegal + r/Entrepreneur threads aggregated on paypalreviews.com
quantified: 180-day holds on $10,000, $44,000 and over $100,000; one thread at 1,361 upvotes / 474 comments
frequency: Recurring; described by the aggregator as the most common complaint by far
notes: Medium strength: large volume of consistent anecdote, no official figures. See section B.

pain: Pay in 4 is denied silently by an automated system - no specific reason, no human able to override, and the option then disappears from checkout, sometimes permanently after a single late payment
audience: PayPal Pay Later users, disproportionately those with thin or damaged credit
quantified: Users reporting 20+ successful plans then permanent denial; 2 years of on-time payment then denied; option gone for 6 months to 2 years; support explicitly says it is fully automated and cannot be overridden
frequency: Very high - a large fraction of recent r/paypal Pay Later threads
notes: Medium-strong: highly consistent across many independent threads over 4 years. See sections D and E.
